```{r Review Video 17}
library(car)

options(contrasts = c("contr.sum","contr.poly"))

covid <- read.csv()

model <- lm(infections ~ block + masks + vaccine, data = covid)
Anova(model, type 3)

library(agricolae)

t1 <- HSD.test(model, trt="mask")
t1$groups

t2 <- HSD.test(model, trt="vaccine")
t2$groups



```

Sometimes Randomization meses up, and even though the designs at right are random, they don't do a good job of controlling spatial variation.

Sometimes to control the error or simplify the experiment, it's fine to sacrifice some randomization. (Restricted randomization)

Ex: Greenhouse treatments - Testing biological seed treatments on maize. - Always pair a treated and an untreated pot. \# We may have one problem with + and - variables, so we can fix one parameter to vary other one.

Ex: Drought tolerance - It's hard to vary irrigation, so we change the hardest parameter.
